messages.author: 40c39176b13a80bb
messages.subject: parboot and unmarkedFitPCO
parts:
I have some avian point count data, 3 replicates per each of 3 years.  After comparing a set of open and closed population models, the best by AIC is an open Poisson model with gamma fixed at 0.  I would like to report some measure of absolute goodness of fit of this model, but the parboot function seems not to work with unmarkedFitPCO objects.  Is there a way to tweak parboot to handle open model fits? 

If such a tweak is problematical, does this line of reasoning work:  The closed Poisson population model with exactly the same covariates as the best open model provides an acceptable fit by parboot on SSE (p = 0.558 with 250 replicates), but the AIC of the gamma-fixed open model (279) is commandingly better than that of the corresponding closed model (291).  Does it follow that the absolute goodness of fit of the open model must be acceptable because its relative fit is much better than the corresponding closed model, which itself shows acceptable absolute fit? 

(Since gamma is fixed at 0 in both models, the only difference between their designs is that omega is fixed at 1 in the closed model, whereas omega is estimated as an additional parameter in the open model.  The closed model therefore seems to qualify as “nested“ within the open model, and the LRT function indicates a significant difference:  Chisq=14.2201, DF=1, Pr(>Chisq)=0.000163.)

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] parboot and unmarkedFitPCO
parts:
that makes sense to me. The open model should fit if it is precisely the same in all other respects, except that it has one additional parameter.
regards
andy

parts: Thanks Andy and Richard for your replies.  I'll contact you separately Richard for the beta.  I just want to mention here that I went back to the Dail-Madsen preprint after my initial post, and was reminded (if I'm reading their section 3.1 correctly) that a likelihood ratio test of closure like the one that I reported isn't quite appropriate. They suggest a little different test. Thanks again.
